findings.title: A final host cancellation hands out an assessment plan or throws the cancellation value
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix exists on the recorded dirty snapshot; this record does not approve a release.
findings.reproduction: Abort the host signal after the assessment step has returned, before the watch callback gives its result to ShareRestore.read. The retained late-assessment-red command records the failing cancelled case; the live callback control passes.
findings.expected: Return kind=stopped, publish no live plan or timing callback, and wipe the unpublished plan. User cancellation is an outcome (CORE-22).
findings.observed: Before remediation the final abort was missed at the library handoff, and the CLI post-await throwIfAborted path threw CANCELLED.
findings.impact: Supported library/CLI cancellation can continue into assessment output or become an error. No incorrect restored entropy or unauthorized spending was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Capture the assessment signal at the shared library boundary, check it before report/handoff, and use the existing finally cleanup. Remove the CLI throwIfAborted duplication.
findings.requiredVerification: Cancelled and live final callback controls; existing share/terminal cancellation tests; Linux PTY. Current focused checks pass, but fix and verification commits are not yet recorded.

findings.title: Rejected selectors can repeat a seed phrase supplied in the wrong field
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix exists on the recorded dirty snapshot; this record does not approve a release.
findings.reproduction: Supply the public BIP39 zero-entropy phrase as an unsupported record mode/format, month, command/help topic or option name. Initial compiled record probes observed echoes; the original branches and migration inventory retain the interpolated messages. No separately timestamped pre-fix privacy command log was retained.
findings.expected: A refusal never repeats untrusted selector text, which may contain private material (CORE-24). Known program-owned option labels remain useful.
findings.observed: Original record/calendar/command refusals interpolated supplied selector text; the unknown-option label fallback returned the supplied name.
findings.impact: An accidental paste or an untyped host routing private text into metadata can copy that text to displayed or retained errors. Local disclosure only was demonstrated with public data; host compromise, shell argument history and intentional exports are outside this fix.
findings.recommendedFix: Use generic unknown-selector messages and avoid coercing rejected objects. Derive known card-option labels from one owned metadata source.
findings.requiredVerification: Seven current privacy regression cases and the compiled contract harness pass. Wider arbitrary text/host-error confidentiality and browser UI behavior are not established.

findings.title: Owned refusals lack stable module codes
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Fix exists on the recorded dirty snapshot; this record does not approve a release.
findings.reproduction: Inventory source/tooling native error construction in the starting dirty tree. The initial source inventory has 500 sites; the automatic migration manifest covers 494 after six pilot replacements, plus 50 tooling sites and the aggregate rollback failure.
findings.expected: Owned errors carry stable module codes, with one owned message source; native kinds, causes and operational failures retain their contracts (CORE-23, TS-06).
findings.observed: Native constructors supplied messages without a stable code, forcing hosts to depend on text.
findings.impact: Fragile front-end error handling and standards nonconformance; no changed cryptographic result was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep code/message definitions with each module, use one ErrorCatalog implementation and suppliedMessage adapter, retain existing specialized errors, and add a source/tooling gate and negative gate fixtures.
findings.requiredVerification: Native error kinds, immutable code, cause and aggregate causes; qualified/unknown/inherited codes; front-end message handling; portable modules and pnpm check pass. The lexical gate is not a proof against every alias or future constructor form.
